inputs.original_text: President Luis Abinader continued his high-level agenda in France this week, centering on the Dominican Republic’s integration into global standards for transparency. On 25 March 2026, Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in Paris, formalizing a partnership to design the country’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy. inputs.modified_text: Abinader’s government has signed an agreement in Paris with OECD chief Mathias Cormann to design the Dominican Republic’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy. Fighting corruption is essential, but it must be done by strengthening the country’s own institutions and demanding accountability from those who govern—not by letting unelected international bureaucrats shape national policy. A country’s standards should serve its people and respect its sovereignty, not simply follow whatever is branded as “global standards.”

rationales.theme_drift: Both versions concern the agreement to develop the Dominican Republic’s first integrity and anti-corruption strategy, though the modified version gives more weight to a sovereignty-focused argument.
rationales.subtopic_drift: The modified text adds institutional strengthening, government accountability, and resistance to international influence, while the original emphasizes transparency and integration into global standards.
rationales.entity_drift: The key country, OECD, and Cormann remain, but the modified text omits Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez and replaces the named signatories’ framing with Abinader’s government.
rationales.relation_drift: The original says Álvarez and Cormann signed the MoU and Abinader witnessed it; the modified text attributes signing to Abinader’s government and Cormann, changing the stated roles.
rationales.contradiction_drift: The modified text contains no clear internal contradiction.
